slides.title: RMS estate: hours, speech and what to decide

scqa: RMS holds 175.0 TiB across databases, an object store and file shares. Scaling what the census read in each folder to every listed folder, the estate most likely holds 500,290.3 hours of media: 190,196.8 hours of speech and 341,566.0 hours of music, estimated separately.

Only 8.5% of the forecast hours rest on files read and judged, and 73.4% sit in buckets the census key cannot read. The ninety-five per cent forecast interval spans 212,923.5 hours, 42.6% of the forecast, and excludes model error.
What does the estate hold, where does its value sit, and what should management decide first?

RMS holds a large multilingual speech and text archive. The whole-estate forecast is 500,290.3 hours of media, with 190,196.8 hours of speech and 341,566.0 hours of music, each with its ninety-five per cent forecast interval in the tables beside. Kiswahili (38,788.1 speech hours), Gikuyu (32,002.9) and Ekegusii (16,729.3) lead. One bucket the key cannot read carries 251,976.0 forecast hours, 50.4% of the estate. The first decision is an object-read grant for the census key, which turns that exposure into measurement. Archive tiering and duplicate reconciliation follow once repriced; a speech-and-text pilot is the earning path to scope.

table.label: How the forecast was built — the donor folders by media kind
table.note: 2,000 seeded simulations over 1,334 folder strata. Measured strata: normal draws around the census estimator and its standard error. Forecast strata: in each simulation a donor folder of the same media kind is drawn — every readable bucket is one witness (bucket weight ∝ √ of its files), its folders share that weight by file count, and a Gaussian kernel on log mean file size (σ = 1.0, widened until at least 3 donors carry weight) favours donors whose files look like the target's; hours = bytes × the donor's seconds per megabyte; speech, music and language hours = hours × the donor's shares. Strata are summed in every simulation; est is the median, lo–hi the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles. Intervals carry sampling and between-folder variation, not model error or the chance that refused buckets differ in kind from every readable one.

receipts.text: Interim tiered content census (content_sample); snapshots OBS 2026-10-03T02:33:28.832346+00:00; NAS 2026-10-03T02:33:24.807604+00:00; receipts cr-9bc59057d47c, cr-aa33fffba60e, cr-bbf71c8d905a, cr-cb0e66bd3e24, cr-cf4eef79995b, cr-f1415e395361 on akki-vm and akki-vm-ii. Resumable listing, header probes of accessible audio and a per-folder video sample (ranged reads → ffprobe), with unprobed durations extrapolated where possible; a seeded stratified sample of files per folder read byte for byte, verified against the listing and judged on every two-second window by the admitted music detector and the current audio language model; ratio estimators with finite-population correction give the 95 % intervals. Listing, probing and sampling are incomplete. Model readings, not human labels; intervals exclude model error and inaccessible or unsampled content.

Whole-estate Monte Carlo forecast over the retained content-census receipts (cr-bbf71c8d905a, cr-cb0e66bd3e24, cr-cf4eef79995b, cr-f1415e395361): 2,000 seeded simulations over 1,334 folder strata. Measured strata: normal draws around the census estimator and its standard error. Forecast strata: in each simulation a donor folder of the same media kind is drawn — every readable bucket is one witness (bucket weight ∝ √ of its files), its folders share that weight by file count, and a Gaussian kernel on log mean file size (σ = 1.0, widened until at least 3 donors carry weight) favours donors whose files look like the target's; hours = bytes × the donor's seconds per megabyte; speech, music and language hours = hours × the donor's shares. Strata are summed in every simulation; est is the median, lo–hi the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles. Intervals carry sampling and between-folder variation, not model error or the chance that refused buckets differ in kind from every readable one.
